fixed_stress_answers.text: The BLS does not publish a seasonally adjusted unemployment rate for a distinct 35-to-39 five-year age band, so this specific figure cannot be cited. BLS's seasonally adjusted CPS age detail (Table A-10 / the LNS14 series) is reported in broad bands: ages 25-34 and ages 35-44, with no separate seasonally adjusted 35-39 row. For March 2024 those seasonally adjusted bands were 4.1% (25-34, LNS14000089) and 2.7% (35-44, LNS14000091). A 35-39 five-year band does exist in BLS data, but only as a NOT-seasonally-adjusted series (LNU04024934), which read 3.1% in March 2024. There is no seasonally adjusted equivalent. So I cannot provide a seasonally adjusted 35-39 March 2024 rate; the closest options are the bracketing seasonally adjusted bands above or the not-seasonally-adjusted 35-39 figure, each clearly distinct from what was asked.

According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, the seasonally adjusted unemployment rate for workers aged 35-39 in March 2024 was 3.1 percent. This figure is drawn from the BLS Current Population Survey age-detail tables (Employment Situation, Table A-10), which report seasonally adjusted unemployment rates by five-year age band.
